name: Difference-and-non-difference (bhedābheda) of Brahman, souls and world

definitions.definition: Brahman is one as cause and many as effect; the souls and world are both different and non-different from it (Bhartṛprapañca: like ocean and waves; Bhāskara: difference through real adjuncts).
The relation is natural (svābhāvika), like snake and coils, sun and rays.
The relation is inconceivable (acintya).

relations.note: Viśiṣṭādvaita's inseparable body–soul relation; Rāmānuja criticised both forms of bhedābheda

definitions.definition: Non-difference of soul and Brahman is natural; difference is due to real limiting adjuncts (body, senses, intellect), removed at liberation after death.
Souls and world are by their very nature both different and non-different from the Lord: different as dependent, atomic and limited; non-different as his powers without separate existence.
Yādavaprakāśa (as reported by Rāmānuja): Brahman itself naturally transforms into Īśvara, souls and matter, and so is both one and many by nature.

The Lord and his powers (internal, marginal, external) are simultaneously one and different, in a way reason cannot resolve and revelation affirms; the soul is his marginal power, a 'difference-and-non-difference manifestation'.
Brahman, pure of māyā, alone is; the world is its real form produced without change; souls are its parts; only saṃsāra is unreal.

relations.note: rejects māyā as the explanation of the world

definitions.definition: Śiva with inseparable cit-śakti is Brahman; souls and world are his body; he is material and efficient cause.

Śrīpati: Śiva (liṅga) qualified by Śakti and the soul (aṅga) qualified by devotion are non-dual; liberation is their union in equal essence (liṅgāṅga-sāmarasya); the Siddhāntaśikhāmaṇi works this out through the stations (sthala).

relations.note: Śrīkaṇṭha's body–soul model vs Śrīpati's Śakti-qualified union; Vīraśaiva authors claim both as their own

name: Brahman's real transformation into the world (pariṇāma)

definitions.definition: The world is a real transformation of Brahman through its power; effect is both different and non-different from cause.
The world is a real transformation of the Lord's power.
Transformation without change (avikṛta).
Transformation of the external power only (śakti-pariṇāma).
Brahman becomes the world while remaining wholly unchanged, as gold in ornaments; creation is manifestation, not change.
Only the external power transforms into the world; the Lord remains unchanged, like the touchstone that yields gold.

name: Combination of knowledge and works (jñāna-karma-samuccaya)

definitions.definition: Liberation is attained by knowledge of Brahman combined with the lifelong performance of one's prescribed duties; works are not abandoned upon knowledge.

notes: Opposed by Śaṅkara and Sureśvara, for whom knowledge alone liberates (see dsp:jnana-karma-samuccaya).

name: The soul as a part (aṃśa) of Brahman

definitions.definition: A part delimited by real adjuncts.
A naturally distinct part and power, dependent on the Lord.
A spark-like part of Brahman with bliss concealed.
A separated part (vibhinnāṃśa) of the marginal power.

name: The atomic size of the self (aṇu-jīva)

definitions.definition: The soul is atomic, a knower, one per body, infinite in number.
The soul is atomic, a spark of Brahman.
The soul is an infinitesimal particle of consciousness.

notes: Nyāya, Sāṃkhya and Advaita hold the self all-pervading (see dsp:atomic-or-pervasive-self).

name: The soul as the Lord's marginal power, his eternal servant

definitions.definition: The soul is Kṛṣṇa's marginal (taṭasthā) power, eternally his servant, able to turn toward the internal power (devotion) or the external (māyā).

name: The three realities: cit, acit, Īśvara (Nimbārka)

definitions.definition: Souls (cit), the non-conscious (acit: aprākṛta, prākṛta, time) and the Lord (Īśvara), all established by scripture.

name: The five things to be known (arthapañcaka, Nimbārka)

definitions.definition: The worshipped, the worshipper, the fruit of grace, the rasa of devotion, the obstacles.

name: The five means (upāya) of the Nimbārka school

definitions.definition: Karma (duty), vidyā (knowledge), upāsanā or dhyāna (meditation), prapatti (surrender to the Lord) and gurūpasatti (surrender to the guru); grace for the humble crowns them.

notes: Listed in the school's manuals (e.g. Vedāntaratnamañjūṣā); exact locus to verify.

name: The three forms of the ultimate in Śuddhādvaita

definitions.definition: Puruṣottama Kṛṣṇa (highest, goal of grace-devotion), Akṣara Brahman (his abode, goal of knowers) and Antaryāmin; the world and souls are further forms — as the Gaṅgā is water, holy river and goddess.

name: Manifestation and concealment of sat, cit and ānanda

definitions.definition: In matter only being is manifest; in souls being and consciousness (bliss concealed); in the Lord all three; creation and dissolution are manifestation and concealment.

name: Brahman as the locus of contradictory attributes

definitions.definition: Contradictory scriptural statements about Brahman are all literally true; it is not necessary to relegate saguṇa statements to a lower level.

relations.note: Vallabha rejects assigning the qualified statements to a lower level

name: The three kinds of souls: puṣṭi, maryādā, pravāha

definitions.definition: Souls are created of three kinds, with different natures and destinies: grace-souls for loving service, rule-souls for scriptural liberation, stream-souls for worldly life.

name: The path of grace (puṣṭi) and the path of rule (maryādā)

definitions.definition: In the maryādā path the Lord gives fruits according to scriptural means; in the puṣṭi path his grace alone gives devotion and service, independent of means and merit.

relations.note: partial analogy: Gauḍīya rule-devotion vs spontaneous devotion (both lineages contrast rule and love)

definitions.definition: The Lord's command to Vallabha at Gokul: by dedicating oneself to Kṛṣṇa in initiation, the five kinds of faults of body and soul are removed, and one becomes fit for service.
The drawing of the soul's attachment from the world into Kṛṣṇa through his play, culminating in forgetfulness of the world and love in separation.
Veda, Gītā, Brahma Sūtra and Bhāgavata, each later one resolving doubts about the earlier.

name: Revelation as the decisive means of knowledge, the Bhāgavata as supreme (Jīva)

definitions.definition: Of the means of knowledge, revelation alone reaches the transcendent; the Bhāgavata, natural commentary on the Brahma Sūtras, is supreme.

relations.note: both make the Bhāgavata the decisive scripture

definitions.definition: One non-dual reality realised in three ways: as Brahman (effulgence, incomplete), Paramātman (indwelling partial expansion) and Bhagavān (full, with all powers); Kṛṣṇa is Bhagavān himself.
Internal (svarūpa/cit), marginal (the souls) and external (māyā) powers; the basis of acintya-bhedābheda.

name: The three aspects of the internal power: hlādinī, sandhinī, saṃvit

definitions.definition: Pleasure, existence and knowledge aspects of the Lord's own power (VP 1.12.69); the essence of hlādinī is love, whose summit is Rādhā.

name: Kṛṣṇa as the Lord himself (svayaṃ bhagavān)

definitions.definition: Kṛṣṇa is the source of all avatāras, not an avatāra of Viṣṇu (BhP 1.3.28 as governing statement).
Puruṣottama Kṛṣṇa is the highest form of Brahman.
Kṛṣṇa is the supreme Brahman with Rādhā.

name: Rādhā as Kṛṣṇa's pleasure-power and supreme devotee

definitions.definition: Rādhā is the hlādinī-śakti, the embodiment of mahābhāva, one in self with Kṛṣṇa yet in a separate body for the play.
Rādhā, daughter of Vṛṣabhānu, is worshipped on Kṛṣṇa's left as his eternal consort.
Rādhā as Svāminī (mistress), emphasised in Viṭṭhalanātha's writings.

name: Caitanya as Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa combined

definitions.definition: Caitanya is Kṛṣṇa who took Rādhā's mood and complexion to taste her love; also the yuga-avatāra of Kali inaugurating the chanting of the name.
Kṛṣṇa as devotee in five aspects: Caitanya, Nityānanda, Advaita, Śrīvāsa, Gadādhara.
Rūpa's classification: svayaṃ-rūpa, tad-ekātma-rūpa (vilāsa, svāṃśa), āveśa; puruṣa, guṇa, līlā, manvantara, yuga and śaktyāveśa avatāras; Kṛṣṇa is their source.
Mahāviṣṇu (Kāraṇodakaśāyin), from whose pores the universes emerge; Garbhodakaśāyin within each universe; Kṣīrodakaśāyin as the Paramātman in every being.

name: The Lord's eternal abode (dhāma: Goloka, Vraja)

definitions.definition: Goloka/Vraja, made of wish-fulfilling gems, is Kṛṣṇa's highest abode above Vaikuṇṭha; the earthly Vraja (Vṛndāvana, Govardhana, Rādhākuṇḍa) is non-different from it.
Vraja and Gokul as the site of the Lord's eternal play into which grace admits the soul.
Kṛṣṇa's play is eternal in the unmanifest abode and becomes manifest on earth once in a day of Brahmā; the parakīyā appearance belongs (for Jīva) to the manifest play.
Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa's pastimes through the eight periods of the day, the object of meditative remembrance.
Mirrored in the eight daily periods of temple service (aṣṭayāma sevā), from maṅgalā to śayana.
Favourable cultivation of Kṛṣṇa free of other desires, uncovered by knowledge and works; causeless (ahaitukī).

name: The six characteristics of pure devotion

definitions.definition: Destroys suffering; bestows auspiciousness; makes liberation trivial; rarely attained; intense special bliss; attracts Kṛṣṇa.
Devotion is threefold: practice, emotion and love; practice aims at the manifestation of the eternally perfect bhāva.

relations.note: prema is then graded further in the Ujjvalanīlamaṇi

definitions.definition: Practice impelled by scriptural command where spontaneous attraction is absent.
Practice following the spontaneous love of the Vraja residents, qualified by eager longing (lobha), performed in the practitioner's body and the inner perfected body; kāmānugā or sambandhānugā.

name: The stages of love from prema to mahābhāva

definitions.definition: prema → sneha → māna → praṇaya → rāga → anurāga → bhāva/mahābhāva (rūḍha, adhirūḍha: modana, mādana).
Śānta, dāsya (prīta), sakhya (preyas), vātsalya and madhura (ujjvala), in ascending intensity; each richer mood includes the qualities of the lower.

relations.note: the classical aesthetic rasas are worldly; Rūpa's are directed to Kṛṣṇa

definitions.definition: Hāsya, adbhuta, vīra, karuṇa, raudra, bhayānaka, bībhatsa, occasional within devotion.
Sthāyibhāva (love for Kṛṣṇa) + vibhāva (ālambana, uddīpana) + anubhāva + sāttvika-bhāva + vyabhicārī-bhāva = rasa.

name: The eight sāttvika signs of ecstasy

definitions.definition: Stambha, sveda, romāñca, svara-bheda, vepathu, vaivarṇya, aśru, pralaya — with degrees from smouldering to blazing.
Transient emotions that surge within the permanent love for Kṛṣṇa.

name: The maidservant's mood (mañjarī-bhāva)

definitions.definition: Summary: the aspiration to serve Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa as one of Rādhā's young maidservants, seeking no union with Kṛṣṇa, taught in Raghunātha Dāsa's Vilāpakusumāñjali and cultivated through the inner perfected identity; its specifics are transmitted by the guru.

notes: Recorded at summary level; the lineages treat detailed identity instruction (siddha-praṇālī) as confidential.

definitions.definition: The spiritual identity in which the practitioner mentally serves in Vraja; distinct from the practitioner's physical body, with which external practice continues.
Compare the 'body fit for service' (sevopayogi-deha), a fruit of service.

Rūpa: the gopīs' paramour love is the summit of amorous rasa; Jīva: they are Kṛṣṇa's own potencies, so svakīyā in truth; Viśvanātha: parakīyā eternally. Love is defined as desire for Kṛṣṇa's pleasure, not one's own.
Rādhā as Kṛṣṇa's eternal consort; the school's view is generally described as svakīyā.

name: Non-difference of the name and the named

definitions.definition: The name is Kṛṣṇa himself, fully empowered, not an ordinary word; it reveals itself to a tongue turned to service.
The name uttered inattentively or with another intent destroys sin and gives liberation (Ajāmila), but only pure chanting gives love; offences block its fruit.

name: The dharma of the Kali age

definitions.definition: Congregational chanting of the name is the dharma of Kali, inaugurated by Caitanya; in Kali there is no other way.
In Kali all paths are ruined; Kṛṣṇa alone is the refuge.
The structure of Caitanya's teaching to Sanātana and of the Ṣaṭ Sandarbha: knowledge of Kṛṣṇa and his powers, devotion as the means, love as the goal.

One initiating guru and many instructing gurus; the Lord within (caitya-guru); the guru is to be honoured as Kṛṣṇa's representative; qualification is knowledge of Kṛṣṇa, not birth; guru and disciple should examine each other.
Initiation is given by the ācārya's descendants (the Gosvāmī houses); the disciple's relation is to the Lord through the guru's family.

name: Love of God as the fifth and highest goal

definitions.definition: Prema surpasses the four aims including liberation; devotees reject the five liberations without service.
Puṣṭi devotees seek service and nirodha, not liberation.
Using things in Kṛṣṇa's service without attachment rather than renouncing them as worldly.

name: The twenty-six qualities of a Vaiṣṇava

definitions.definition: Kindness, truthfulness, equality, mildness, freedom from pride, dependence on Kṛṣṇa alone and the rest.
Sin not yet fructifying, latent, as seed and about to fructify are destroyed in sequence by devotion; even prārabdha yields.

name: The devotee's indifference to powers and liberation

definitions.definition: Those who desire enjoyment, liberation or powers are restless; the devotee is desireless and so at peace.
The 'supernatural capacity' given by grace is capacity to relish the Lord, not yogic power.
Inner absorption (antar-daśā), half-external (ardha-bāhya) and external (bāhya) consciousness, alternating in his last years of divine madness.
Separation (vipralambha) intensifies love; Caitanya's last years and Śikṣāṣṭaka 7–8.
Love in separation is the highest state; renunciation is fitting only when viraha makes home impossible.

name: Śiva as the small space in the heart

definitions.definition: The dahara of Chāndogya 8.1 is Śiva, the supreme ether that is his cit-śakti.
Liberation as equality with Śiva in bliss and powers except world-governance.

name: Equal authority of Veda and Śaiva Āgama

definitions.definition: Both proceed from Śiva; Śrīkaṇṭha sees no difference between them.
Non-difference with Brahman after death, once the adjuncts have fallen.
Attainment of the Lord's nature in non-separation, with the soul's distinctness preserved; by grace.
Maryādā souls attain union (sāyujya) or Akṣara; puṣṭi souls receive service in the Lord's play, valued above liberation.
Freedom from māyā is a by-product; the goal is prema-service in Kṛṣṇa's abode; sāyujya is rejected.
Equality with Śiva.
Denied by Bhāskara.
Redefined as the state of one who serves Hari in all conditions.
Remembering or uttering the name at death saves even a sinner (Ajāmila); Haridāsa died with the name and Caitanya's form before him.
